# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Age:** In his sixties  <sub>[v2 c1 P25](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0025), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c38 P0](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P14](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0014)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** J. A.  <sub>[v2 c1 P1](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0001), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015)</sub>; James A.  <sub>[v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013), [v2 c5 P13](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Pettifer is a short, heavy-set, bald man with a round face, large blue eyes, and a hairless scalp bordered by a small fringe around his ears. When enraged, his face turns violet and his eyes bulge.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022)_

## Personality

Mr. Pettifer is an outspoken, stubborn, and eccentric man who boasts of speaking his mind directly. Though prone to outbursts of temper and known for being stingy, he possesses a soft-hearted, lonely, and friendly side. He takes pleasure in storytelling and enjoys young, lively company.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c1 P25](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0025), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)_

## Traits

- Outspoken and candid  <sub>[v2 c1 P25](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0025), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>
- Stubborn  <sub>[v2 c3 P43](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0043)</sub>
- Eccentric  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Stingy  <sub>[v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008)</sub>
- Short-tempered  <sub>[v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013)</sub>
- Sensitive about his baldness  <sub>[v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022)</sub>

## Abilities

- Skilled negotiator  <sub>[v2 c25 P5](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0005)</sub>
- Excellent tea-maker  <sub>[v2 c3 P34](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0034)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep cattle and intruders out of his oat crops  <sub>[v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015)</sub>
- To enjoy quiet, orderly, and friendly company without fuss  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

## History

After moving to Brierley, Mr. Pettifer acquired a reputation as an eccentric bachelor and a recluse who refused women near his home and disliked church donations. When Nell Harcourt's Jersey cow repeatedly trespassed into his oats, he confronted her in a fury. Upon learning the cow was sold by mistake, he accepted Nell's apology, accepted her homemade cake, and traded cows with her, forming a warm friendship with her. Later, he attempted to buy a dress for Nell at a local store but ended up awkwardly buying brown sugar and a rake instead due to his shyness around female clerks. He eventually enlisted Mrs. Sowerby's help to secretly purchase and sew a new dress with puffed sleeves for Nell as a Christmas gift. When his estranged wife, Emily, arrived unexpectedly in Brierley after seeing a newspaper rumor about him, they reconciled, and she restored immaculate order to his house. During a lightning storm, his house was struck and his parrot Nutmeg was killed. He supported the Village Improvement Society and later traded cows with Nell again after another straying incident.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013), [v2 c1 P16](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0016), [v2 c3 P21](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0021), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P35](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0035), [v2 c3 P46](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0046), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c5 P13](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0013), [v2 c5 P24](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0024), [v2 c5 P27](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0027), [v2 c6 P24](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0024), [v2 c25 P5](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0005), [v2 c25 P11](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0011), [v2 c25 P20](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0020), [v2 c25 P24](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0024), [v2 c25 P27](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0027)_

## Background by volume

- Formerly lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, before moving to Brierley  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Kept house with his sister until her death
- Married Emily Scott, a former schoolteacher, but separated after arguments over housecleaning and his swearing parrot
- Inherited a profanely vocal parrot named Nutmeg from his seafaring brother  <sub>[v2 c1 P10](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0010), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038)</sub>
- Purchased Robert Bell's farm in Brierley  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m a crabbed, lonesome, crusty old chap, but I feel young again because of something about that little girl . . . and having that sensation repeated once in a while is something I’d like, since it’s so pleasant.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> Tut, tut, miss, do not utter a single further word regarding it. It is immaterial . . . utterly immaterial. Misfortunes are bound to occur.  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023)</sub>

> There is nothing wrong with my fence. A demonic cow of that sort could not be contained even by the prison fence.  <sub>[v2 c1 P18](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0018)</sub>
